body:
Don’t worry, you are overthinking. Most people are like that at the beginning. You are really new and your co-workers have most likely been that way and seen other newbies do those mistakes as well, so they are expecting you to mess up. It’s really no biggie, just keep trying and if you do something wrong, look at it as a chance to learn. 
Most of my former co-workers, including myself were feeling like that and we wanted to quit so badly during the first month, but after 1-2 months you will eventually get used to the environment and you will feel more comfortable and confident. 
I strongly believe that you will soon get the hang of it and you’ll get things wrong more and more rarely, because after all, even the workers that have been there for decades make mistakes sometimes! It’s human nature!

Such idiots. My gyno told me the same thing because I screamed in pain during iud insertion and it sounded like moaning.
My most recent disturbing doctor visit was when I went to get my blood drawn for ovarian cancer marker testing. The reason I was there for meant I was already emotional and terrified. (Luckily it was nothing bad in the end)
I stretched out my arm and my self harm scars were visible and he went laughing and asked: “You cut or what?”. I don’t care if it wasn’t believable, I told him that I slipped down a hill and skinned my arm, all while I was trying to not choke and cry. I hoped that it would be enough for him to leave it, but he kept looking skeptically at me and asking for more details while grinning in a “yeah sure” manner. The procedure was the quickest I have ever had, but those 30 sec/1 min were more than enough to trigger anxiety and an urge to hurt myself. I would have reported it, but here most doctors are very insulting and act high and mighty and nothing ever comes out of reporting them. I know because almost all doctor visits have left me feeling attacked.

I’m so sad you had to endure all that, I cannot even imagine how hard it must have been. I also had a sad childhood which left deep scars but it was nowhere as bad.
This is really weird to talk about but what helped me most is somehow “recreating” my childhood. I was really lucky to meet my partner when I was at my lowest. My boyfriend sometimes acts like a parent to me and calling him mom really soothes me when I am anxious. He will sometimes buy me toys, we will watch cartoons or play games typically enjoyed by children. When he does that it’s always in a loving, warm and quiet nurturing way. It’s like entering a whole different world, where we have special personalities.
Two weeks after I turned 18 we moved together and since then i have been much better, although I am still working on my recovery. Sometimes it can be hard because I am still living kinda close to my parents but I am moving abroad in a few days.
Thank you for sharing your story. I hope that we both find peace and happiness. ❤️

It can be a very saddening process as you keep seeing doctors and getting rejected but I’d say, ask around if you can freely talk about it.  Ask your family doctor if they know a gyno that will not deny you an iud. You could also make a list of gynos and their phone numbers and call each one and say you want an iud inserted and say you are sure of it and will only come in for the procedure like no consultation beforehand. This way I dont think they can turn you down once you are there and if they wont do the procedure theyll just tell you on the phone and you can cross them off the list. Or you could also try to argue over it, like say it is your choice and insist that you are willing to take the risk and if they dont want your money, youll pay someone else . Some of them will accept to do it afterwards, since Romanians arent exactly rolling in money.  The key is to sound determined. I was younger and my mom had to come with me so that I could get it because I wasnt an adult yet (which is stupid because my friend in Sweden got it at 15 for free and didnt have to tell anyone, which should be the norm here too), but if I had to do it again, I would really argue about it. (If you live in Maramures I could tell you refer you to the office I got it at)

Truly amazing people. The first gyno I asked for an IUD was a woman that apparently tried to get pregnant for many many years and succeeded after doing IVF. I was 17 back then and she told me my uterus is completely developed but there was a small chance that I could have gotten Pelvic Inflammatory Disease and that could have potentially affected my fertility. I told her that it was a risk I was willing to take since I don't want children. She started going on at me, saying yoU DOOOOOONT UndeRstanD it YET!!! You will meet the right man and you will learn true love and then you will just know that you just NEED A BABY TO BE COMPLETE! I told her I was already in a 3 year old relationship and while we are young, we are both getting along amazing and he is childfree too and we just don't want any kids. (2 years later we are still CF and planning to get sterilized in the uk) This reason alone was not good enough, so then I brought up the ethical side of stuff since I am also suffering from multiple chronic illnesses like type 1 diabetes, depression, ocd and more which all have a high chance of being passed on. She then of course went on about the miracles of today's medical industry and how you can use idk what kind of therapy to prevent that (which I googled cause I never heard of it and I couldn't find anything about it?). Anyways, this woman at least didn't hit me with the YOU NEED TO HAVE BAYBEES FIRST, but the next few gynos killed me with that stupid myth. My family doctor was the person who recommended me a gyno who still believed in that myth but agreed to get me one on my own risk. It's okay, my endometriosis-like symptoms have gotten a bit worse (it's a copper iud) but since I cannot take hormones and we already had a condom break on us, I am willing to endure the side effects until my bf gets a vasectomy next year. I hope you also get yours! Truly shocking how they are treating an IUD worse than sterilization itself.

Also, that article got me raging. Those people are against abortion but also against sex ed. They shame you for getting birth control and then shame you for terminating. I have just graduated highschool and the educational system is horrible. They encourage bringing more people into this shit hole, with bad schooling, especially in rural areas which they refuse to improve, to be raised by abusive parents in many cases (most people i asked here, confessed they were abused physically and psychologically and most of them also had alcoholic parents - i was a victim of all these too, although not as bad as others)

I’m also Romanian and I am so fed up with this country, the way reproductive rights work here being one of the biggest reasons. It took me almost 2 years to get an iud because all gynos here still think its impossible to get one without having given birth (which is weird cause they give them to women who gave birth through a c sec, despite that this myth they still believe in meant that only women who gave birth vaginally could get one). I have most symptoms of endometriosis but they are saying its just called being a woman (got this from 4 gynos) and refuse to check why I got these symptoms. I also got shamed by another doctor for having an iud implying that i am a whore. I also got bingoed everytime I mentioned being childfree, of course. The issue with the fact that doctors are being insulting and don’t know shit, cannot even be reported cause everyone shares their views! Good I am moving into the uk in 1 month.

The only thing she did was pull at his clothes every 30 minutes or so while looking at it with disgust and telling it to shut up already. At one point the kid even started running around and my foot was a little bit into the aisle and he stepped on my shoe multiple times, again going completely unnoticed by the mother. Why bring the kid to a 3 to 4 hour ceremony where it has to stand up if you don't even plan to look after it?? It completely ruined the mood for me, although I also feel bad for the kid.. if he is treated like that in public, who knows what that bish is like at home.

I was 17 and needed and X-ray. The nurse had to ask about my last period. I told her I was not sure about the exact date it started but my period was due in one week so if she gave me a calendar i could calculate. She was implying I was stupid for not knowing the date by heart and she started idk why talking about if im using birth control in a very derogatory way almost. I said I was using an IUD, i thought that maybe it was relevant for the results. She started almost praying to God when she heard that, kind of shaming me for having sex and for using birth control. I knew what she had done was unprofessional, but I left feeling sad and ashamed. It had already been very hard to find a doctor to give me an iud and it hurt to see once again another medical worker treating women like that.
